classification.difficultyReason: Reflect four different graph types while transferring intercepts, endpoints and asymptotes.

spec.description: Unshaded Cartesian graph with a blue increasing straight line and arrowheads at both ends.
spec.mathematics: The supplied line passes through (-1/2,0) and (0,1).
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied function and its labelled intercepts are visible.

answer.short: An increasing straight line through $(0,-\tfrac12)$ and $(1,0)$.
answer.worked: Reflect the supplied graph in $y=x$. The intercepts $(-\tfrac12,0)$ and $(0,1)$ become $(0,-\tfrac12)$ and $(1,0)$. Draw the straight line through these points.

spec.description: Solid blue inverse, dashed blue supplied line and black dashed reflection line.
spec.mathematics: The inverse is the reflection of y=2x+1, passing through (0,-1/2) and (1,0).
spec.answerVisibility: Complete inverse sketch appears only in the answer.

spec.description: Unshaded increasing concave-up blue curve, with a horizontal dashed asymptote and continuation arrows.
spec.mathematics: The curve passes through (0,2) and approaches y=1 from above as x decreases. Bézier coordinates describe the schematic shape; no unsupplied equation is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied graph, asymptote and y-axis labels are visible.

answer.short: An increasing, concave-down curve through $(2,0)$, with vertical asymptote $x=1$ and domain $x>1$.
answer.worked: Reflect the curve in $y=x$. The point $(0,2)$ becomes $(2,0)$, and the horizontal asymptote $y=1$ becomes the vertical asymptote $x=1$. The inverse is increasing and concave down on $x>1$.

spec.description: Solid inverse curve, dashed supplied curve, dashed reflection line and vertical inverse asymptote.
spec.mathematics: Every control point of the supplied schematic curve is reflected by interchanging coordinates. The inverse passes through (2,0) and has asymptote x=1.
spec.answerVisibility: Complete inverse sketch appears only in the answer.

spec.description: Unshaded increasing concave-down blue curve beginning on the x-axis and continuing to the right.
spec.mathematics: Endpoint (-4,0), point (0,2), domain x>=-4 and range y>=0. Bézier geometry preserves the schematic shape without assuming an unprinted function rule.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied curve and labelled intercepts are visible.

answer.short: An increasing, concave-up curve beginning at $(0,-4)$ and passing through $(2,0)$; domain $[0,\infty)$.
answer.worked: Reflect the curve in $y=x$. The endpoint $(-4,0)$ becomes $(0,-4)$, and $(0,2)$ becomes $(2,0)$. Sketch the increasing, concave-up reflected curve for $x\geq0$.

spec.description: Solid blue inverse with its included endpoint, dashed supplied curve and black dashed reflection line.
spec.mathematics: The entire schematic path is reflected coordinate by coordinate. The inverse begins at (0,-4), passes through (2,0), and has domain [0,infinity).
spec.answerVisibility: Complete inverse sketch appears only in the answer.

spec.description: Two unshaded blue branches with continuation arrows, black axes and dashed asymptotes.
spec.mathematics: Asymptotes x=1 and y=2. The lower-left branch passes through (0,0); the upper-right branch lies in x>1, y>2. The unprinted function rule is not assumed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied branches, asymptotes and labels are visible.

answer.worked: Reflect both branches in $y=x$. The vertical asymptote $x=1$ becomes $y=1$, and the horizontal asymptote $y=2$ becomes $x=2$. The origin remains fixed. Draw one decreasing branch in $x<2$, $y<1$, through the origin, and the other in $x>2$, $y>1$.

spec.description: Solid inverse branches and black dashed inverse asymptotes; dashed blue supplied branches and their asymptotes provide comparison.
spec.mathematics: All supplied schematic path coordinates are interchanged. The inverse has asymptotes x=2 and y=1 and passes through the origin.
spec.answerVisibility: Complete inverse sketch appears only in the answer.
